data.name: Gaveshan
data.gender_notes: Gaveshan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Gaveshan is derived from Sanskrit words ‘gave’ meaning 'giver' and ‘eshana’ meaning 'treasure'. This name is bestowed upon a child who is believed to bring wealth and prosperity to the family. The name Gaveshan carries the meaning “Giver of Treasure” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gaveshan usually hope their child will grow to embody giver of treasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who bestows wealth and prosperity.
data.etymology: Gaveshan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Giver of Treasure.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gaveshan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gaveshan holds great cultural significance in Hindu society. It is a name that carries the expectation of bestowing wealth and prosperity upon the family. It is a name of great honor as the giver of treasures is often seen as a benefactor and a source of strength and support.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Gaveshan symbolizes the divine gift of giving. It is a reminder of the importance of selfless giving and the power it holds to create a positive impact on the world. The name also embodies the Hindu belief in the abundance of the universe and the idea that material wealth is not a hindrance to spiritual growth, but rather a means to support it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Gaveshan signifies the one who invites or bestows knowledge and wisdom upon others. It is a reminder to be a source of enlightenment and understanding in the lives of those around us.

historical_references.reference: Gaveshan is mentioned as a Hindu king in the inscriptions of the 13th century Chalukyan king, Ballala II.
Another reference to Gaveshan is found in the 15th century inscriptions of the Vijayanagara Empire. He is mentioned as a feudatory chief of the empire.
